name: The Bull River Prowler
text: [overview] A moderate route for stable snow, perhaps comparable in scale to Dragon Tail Peak's Triple Couloirs.
[overview] Traverse left on a snowy ledge, up a rightward runnel to the lower snowfield, then up-left to a couloir zigzagging right to the band of rock higher up.
[overview] a chimney choked with snow may be the crux.
[overview] Dig through the cornice to the summit ridge.

[approach] In winter the road to the Granite Lake trailhead near Libby is unplowed past the end of the pavement, so the trip starts on skis or foot or by snowmobile and is long, then the trail follows Granite Creek to the lake.
[approach] The couloirs funnel snow, so check the avalanche forecast.
[approach] the firmest snow is on the debris fan it deposits.
earlierWhy: Winter snow couloir route in the Cabinets with cornices; no glacier travel.

name: The Stumbling Stone
text: [approach] Stay to climber's right of the feature called Thunderdome and follow the obvious gully and snow slope.
earlierWhy: Summer rock route in the Cabinets reached by a gully and snow slope; no glacier, snow persistence unclear.

name: Unprotected Fourplay
earlierWhy: Winter ice and mixed route with steep snow on a Cabinets face; no glacier travel.

name: North Face
text: [overview] Get going early, since cornices can break from the summit ridge above.
[overview] Steep neve and WI3 for several pitches lead to a rock band, where two pitches of M4-5, and maybe one M6 move, follow.
[overview] Work left (east) when possible to get out from beneath the 40' cornices 800' above, then go 700' straight up more steep neve.
[approach] The face carries cornices on the summit ridge above, which is why parties start early.
earlierWhy: Steep neve and ice with cornices in winter; could not confirm the face carries no glacier.

name: Memento Mori
earlierWhy: No text, and a search found nothing about this line, so neither fact could be checked.

name: Stella by Starlight
text: [overview] A serious mixed line up the Wheeler Peak headwall above the cirque: snow and ice to a ramp, wet rock beside a water gully, aid through dripping overhangs, then a long icy ramp trending left to exit just below the summit.
[detailed_rack] Bring snow and ice anchors, plus stoppers, hexes and thin pitons for rock.
earlierWhy: Wheeler's cirque holds a small glacier reported to have crevasses at the headwall, and the route starts on snow and ice there.

name: Full Richardson
text: [overview] Up a distinct couloir on the North Face: two WI2/3 steps and about 300 ft of moderate snow lead to the 30m crux, steep aerated ice with poor gear but great axe sticks, behaving more like alpine than water ice.
[overview] A picket above the curtain makes the belay;
[overview] Moderate snow in the bowl follows, around 600 feet to the summit;
[overview] Snow steepens under the summit block and may be loose at the very top;
[detailed_rack] Screws (with stubbies) and pickets.
[approach] Two short steps of ice or snow, depending on the season, come first, then moderate snow leads up the couloir.
[approach] Watch the snow stability here and check the avalanche forecast.
earlierWhy: North face couloir on a glaciated peak, but text never says whether a crevassed glacier is crossed.

name: Nine O'clock Gully
text: [overview] It needs deep snow to be in shape and might carry a cornice.
[descent_text] Either gully needs solid snow cover to be in condition, and a cornice may cap the top of this one, so look it over from below before committing.
earlierWhy: Winter snow gully needing deep cover; the text does not say whether a glacier is on the line.

name: West Rib
text: [overview] The lower ridge is moderate snow;
[overview] Protection is rarely needed until the pinnacle, so most parties carry a few pickets or screws for the snow and a light rack of nuts and slings for the top.
earlierWhy: A west-side ridge route with moderate snow lower down and no glacier crossing.

name: Iron Maiden
text: [detailed_rack] Thin conditions call for pins and nuts, while fat ones may allow screws and an occasional picket.
earlierWhy: Ice climb on Illumination Rock; the text does not describe the approach.

name: North Milk Creek Glacier
text: [overview] Climbed as a gully, since the glacier has likely melted away.
[overview] Quick going on firm snow, and among the shortest ways up the mountain from the trailhead.
earlierWhy: The glacier has likely melted; climbed as a snow gully.

name: East Buttress
text: [overview] The lower part opens with an ice pillar at the toe, probably the crux (snow ramps substitute if it is not formed), then skirts a big buttress on the right, edges left to the crest, scrambles, and follows the narrowing crest across a gendarme to tower number tw
earlierWhy: Winter ice and mixed line; glacier crossing not stated.

name: Instruct Me How to Douglas
earlierWhy: No text; a winter ice and mixed line with unknown glacier exposure.

name: Devil's Kitchen Headwall (DKH) - Left Variation
text: [detailed_rack] With fat ice and consolidated snow above, take pickets and medium-length screws.

[approach] The route climbs the long couloir splitting the middle of the Devil's Kitchen Headwall: go up the snow and debris slope below the headwall into the couloir's entrance, then steep snow to the first ice step.
earlierWhy: Snow and ice couloir; approach glacier status not stated.

name: Devil's Kitchen Headwall (DKH) - Right Variation
text: [overview] It sits in the corner formed by the headwall and Steel Cliffs, and starts on moderate snow.
[detailed_rack] Kit varies with conditions: 2-3 pickets, ice screws.
[detailed_rack] Early June brought rotten ice-snow on the upper steepening, and firm snow lower, in the runnels.
[approach] The route is tucked into the angle where the headwall above the Devil's Kitchen runs into the Steel Cliffs, and begins on moderate snow.
earlierWhy: Moderate snow start; approach glacier status not stated.

name: Flying Buttress (DKH V3)
text: [overview] This variant has milder ice than the standard lines and finishes on the upper Wyeast route, with its steep snow crux and exposed gendarme.
[overview] Climb easy ice or moderate snow in the gully toward an apparent dead-end headwall.
[overview] Near its top, go right up an obvious snow ramp to the Wyeast ridge crest, then left along it past a small saddle where DKH V2 joins and a short traverse that may be the crux.
[overview] Moderate to steep, exposed snow follows, easing toward the summit.
[detailed_rack] Bring two tools, or one tool and an axe, plus pickets and a few ice screws if pitching.
earlierWhy: Snow and ice gully; glacier crossing not stated.

name: Men of Steel
earlierWhy: No text; an ice line with unknown approach.

name: East Buttress
text: [gear] Ice axe and crampons (seasonal).
earlierWhy: Little text; only seasonal ice axe and crampons mentioned.
